headline: Two mainnet rehearsals, then attacker code ran on Binance 14 for 3 hours 49 minutes
dek: LunarCrush checked every transaction cited in posts against Ethereum mainnet through public nodes and Blockscout. The chain shows an eighteen-hour build-up, one valid authorization out of fifty, and a delegation that kept sweeping for nearly four hours.

key_numbers.label: sweeper v1 deployed, 18 hours before the drain
rehearsals on the attacker's own wallets (13:51, 16:20)
Binance 14 under attacker code until 00:10 UTC

narrative: The operator address, 0x7C86…5CA0, has a history that fits on one screen. Three withdrawals from the Tornado Cash 0.1 ETH pool funded it: Oct 28 at 07:39 and 08:53 UTC, and Oct 29 at 08:23. Two sibling wallets were funded the same way in the same 31 hours: 0xFD41 (0.1 ETH at 01:15 Oct 29) and 0xe4F9 (0.1 ETH at 07:08, then 0.994 ETH from the 1 ETH pool at 14:54). About 1.49 ETH from the mixer funded the whole operation.

@spreekaway's first post at 20:32 said the contract call 'was funded by Tornado Cash'. That was correct, and it was the detail that led on-chain readers to treat the move as hostile rather than housekeeping.

The preparation was public for eighteen hours. At 02:28:59 UTC on Oct 29 the operator deployed a first sweeper contract (0x19be…f2bf, never verified). At 13:51 it sent two type-4 (EIP-7702) transactions delegating two fresh wallets it controlled, 0x8378 and 0x9C29, to that contract. From 13:57, 0xFD41 funded them with 0.001 and 0.002 ETH and seeded them with a few dollars of USDT and USDC. At 14:19:59 and 14:24:11 the operator swept both; the internal calls touched DAI, USDC and USDT.

Posts reconstructed the rehearsal 67 minutes after the sweep: @MetaFinancialAI had the timeline by 21:31, @danupsher summarized it at 21:47 ('rehearsed this afternoon on 2.54 USDT'), and @Aytunc described the test addresses at 22:06.
At 15:59:11 the operator deployed the contract it would use, 0x63e8…6fAe. Its code lets only 0x7C86 call sweep, withdraw or an execute passthrough, and its sweep leaves exactly 1 ETH behind.

From 16:20 it ran the full sequence on a third test wallet, 0x43AE: delegate (16:20:47 and 16:25:59), fund with 1.01 ETH from 0xe4F9 (16:24), sweep (16:30:11, 0.01 ETH out), withdraw (16:47:23, 1.0 ETH back to 0xe4F9). At 18:20:47, 0xe4F9 sent the operator 1.082 ETH, funding for the real run. @0xQuit's 21:09 reconstruction (492K engagements) had the deploy time and four-step sequence right; @blockaid_ posted the contract address and hardcoded operator at 21:25.

The delegation is transaction 0xad99…298b at 20:20:59 UTC: a type-4 transaction from the operator to Binance 14 (0x28C6…1d60) carrying 50 authorizations. Decoded from a public node, all 50 point to the same delegate on chain 1, their nonces run in sequence, and every signature recovers to Binance 14's key.

An EIP-7702 authorization applies only if its nonce equals the signer's current nonce. Binance 14 was sending several transactions a block, and its live nonce when the tuples were processed was 18914809. That tuple applied and the other 49 were skipped. Binance 14's next own transaction, at 20:21:11, carried 18914810. Exactly one authorization took effect.

An authorization signs a different message from a transaction, so these fifty could not have been harvested from the wallet's withdrawal traffic; they were produced as authorizations. @0xQuit reached a related conclusion at 21:21 ('likely the attacker collected all 50 over some period of time'), as did @blockaid_ at 21:50 ('the hot wallet was still firing. One nonce in that window landed'). A stolen key, a compromised signing service and a deceived signing step all fit the record.

Seventeen blocks later, at 20:24:23, the operator called sweep on Binance 14. The receipt holds 63 Transfer events from 63 token contracts plus the ETH move, matching the '167,464 ETH + 63 tokens' @odysseas_eth posted at 20:54. Everything went to 0x5227…2f8c, which Etherscan later labeled 'Binance Hot Wallet Exploiter 2'. The ten largest lines the explorer shows for this first sweep: 1.615B USDT, 62.6M RLUSD, 29,934 wBETH, 11,372 XAUt, 6.19M UNI, 27.8M USD1, 198M ENA, 7.18T PEPE, 2.26M LINK and 128K AAVE.

The sweep cost 0.000414 ETH (2,455,349 gas at 0.17 gwei), about $0.93. At 20:41:23 the operator used the execute passthrough to send a call from Binance 14 to 0xEe7a…4055, an ERC-1967 proxy that posts called 'Hot Wallet 34'. It already trusted Binance 14 as a permitted caller and released 780M USDC to 0x5227; @kethcode had the owner relationship by 22:08. At 20:59:47 another 43M USDC came the same way.

The code stayed on Binance 14 for 3 hours 49 minutes, until 00:10:35 on Oct 30, when the account signed its own authorization pointing at the zero address. That clears the code; it does not rotate the key or revoke token allowances, and it holds until another valid authorization is included on-chain; clearing the code does not invalidate authorizations already signed. Throughout the window Binance 14 kept sending its own transactions (its own transactions ran from nonce 18914810 to 18914903): the key holder kept control, and the account also ran the attacker's code.

The attacker swept again at 21:04 (3.9M USDT plus dust), at 21:44 (200.4M USDT, 6,591 LINK, 7,008 UNI and others) and at 22:39 (POL, GRT, SKY, SENT, ENSO, XUSD, STRK, FF, CAKE and SYN, at least $7.5M on the ten largest lines the explorer lists) to a second receiver, 0xA97b. Six more sweeps between 23:36 and 23:56 returned nothing.

Value kept arriving. Blockscout records 533 incoming token transfers to Binance 14 between 20:24 and 00:10, including 205.7M USDT, 180B PEPE and 859M SHIB. The 1 ETH floor in the sweep logic paid gas for the wallet's own outgoing transactions, so Binance 14 kept transacting and looked normal. @uttam_singhk described it at 22:00: 'The wallet stayed operational and kept receiving deposits the attacker could take again.'
After the revocation, Binance 14's own outgoing transfers of USDT, SingularityNET, PlayDapp and WLFI between 00:47 and 01:53 failed with status 'error' and no revert reason.

callouts.title: The posts were right, and early
callouts.body: Every on-chain claim checked in the sampled posts held up, and fast: the sweep was public in 8 minutes, the 780M USDC pull in 7, the delegation in 33 and the fifty authorizations in 60. Only the totals varied.

receipts.quote: The attacker didn't know Binance 14's live nonce. So they sprayed 50 EIP-7702 auths (18914775-18914824) in one type-4 tx. Only 1 of 50 was a hit.
...was rehearsed this afternoon on 2.54 USDT. Same operator EOA. Same sweep() selector. Same drainer kit.
The attacker left Binance wallet exactly 1.00 ETH after every sweep... The wallet stayed operational and kept receiving deposits the attacker could take again
Binance 14 was the owner of Hot Wallet 34. once the sweeper could run as Binance 14, it could use that existing permission to pull another $823m USDC out of wallet 34.
20:20:59 UTC: delegation installed. 20:24:23: another address calls sweep(). 7702 lets a normal wallet execute delegated code.

watch: Binance's post-mortem on how fifty authorizations came to be signed by Binance 14's key.
The receivers 0x5227 and 0xA97b: at 03:20 UTC 0x5227 held 16,501 ETH and was still swapping long-tail tokens into ETH.
Binance 14's failed transfers after 00:47 UTC (USDT, SingularityNET, PlayDapp, WLFI): whether they become user-facing withdrawal delays.
